_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Double Dragon (ADR-0239, F14.18).
Rung used: ADR-0239 s1's second - a published RAM selector pinned for the
run - because the game has no stage select of its own. The title's MODE A/B
menu picks one or two players and nothing else, and the only in-game way to
another stage is to finish the one before it. Rung 3 (a save state reached
by search, chain or movie) is out of this slice's scope.
Three facts this profile had to measure. None is guessable and all of them
are on this checkout's dump (mint-city-slum.txt records each one):
1. $003D does select the stage, and the selection is a real warp: pinning it
at 0x00-0x03 makes the game load a different one of the four stages the
manual's Game Stages list names - City Slum, Industrial Area, Forest,
Hideout of the Boss. Measured by drawing, not by the byte: the four
sessions of the sweep write different material, and the byte in RAM still
reads 00/01/02/04 afterwards - a cheat substitutes the value the CPU
reads and never writes memory - so $003D can NOT be the session's RAM
check. It would read its own pin, and on value 03 it does not even do
that.
2. The pin is held for the WHOLE run, and that was measured rather than
assumed. The vendored database's own words for these codes are
"(disable after stage begins)", so "pinned for the run" is a claim that
had to be tested. Probe release_test.py holds the pin across the read and
then releases it, the only way the recorder offers (mint the entry WITH
the pin, then start the session from that state with no cheat at all),
and the released arm does not keep the stage: all four values end the
120 s session back on the City Slum's level-data pointer ($0018 = 5CC0),
while the arm that holds the pin ends on the stage it selected. The
identity value 00 is the control that makes that readable: released, it
is byte-identical to the held arm (0 of 2048 RAM bytes differ), so the
reversion on 01-03 is the pin's absence and not the release machinery.
The game reads $003D again later in the session - which is what the
database's warning is about - and a release before that second read
loses the selection. See runs/f1418/doubledragon/RESULT.md.
3. $0018/$001A is the check. It is a 16-bit pointer into PRG page $C0 that
reads $C05C/$C060, $C065/$C071, $C07D/$C085 and $C0E1/$C0ED on the four
stages, and it is the level-data pointer of the stage the game loaded:
the two runs of the same entry that differ only in the pinned value are
byte-identical through frame 103 and diverge at frame 104, and $0018
has already taken that stage's value by frame 106 - 2 frames after the
read, 4 after the pin's first effect. From there to the end of a 120 s
session it does not move: 24 state readings (four values x the entry's
last frame, 30, 60, 90 and 120 s on one body, and 120 s on a second,
different body) hold the same pointer, and probe/check_candidates.py
finds 33 bytes that are constant within a stage and distinct across the
four with $0018's the one that survives every body. It is NOT in either
published source - neither names a level-data pointer - so it was found
by diffing the four stages' states. It is a check, not a cheat, so
ADR-0184 s5's "no code is invented" does not bite; what it does mean is
that the check is only as good as this measurement, and the measurement
is in the probe rather than in a citation.
The Code/Data Logger was run for all four stages (probe/cdl_pointer.py)
to test whether the pointer really names the stage's own data. It is
suggestive and NOT a proof: the byte each pointer names is logged Data
during its own stage's run, and banks 0 and 6 are exclusive to value 00
and bank 2 to value 02, but the fixed bank 7 logs all four as Data for
every stage, so the CDL cannot separate them. The proof used is the
behavioural one above.
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.

navigation.source: Almar's Guides, "Double Dragon Action Replay Codes (USA)" (https://www.almarsguides.com/retro/walkthroughs/nes/games/DoubleDragon/ActionReplay/, fetched 2026-09-26 with curl -sL, HTTP 200): "Level Select: 003D:??" with "Level Select - Stage 1: 003D:00", "Level Select - Stage 2: 003D:01", "Level Select - Stage 3: 003D:02" and "Level Select - Stage 4: 003D:03". The same three non-identity codes are in this checkout's vendored database, UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json, under "Double Dragon (USA)" as "Start on mission 2 (disable after stage begins)" = 003D:01, mission 3 = 003D:02 and mission 4 = 003D:03. The two sources agree on the address, the values and their order; the vendored database's ROM identity is NOT inherited here (it files a different dump, SHA1 91B3B33A4E24D5DD1A5AFA480B8C44FAC503E926 - see stage-set.json's note). The four places the values reach are the manual's Game Stages: City Slum, Industrial Area, Forest, Hideout of the Boss.

_entryComment: One entry for all four values, because the pin is the whole of what
selects the place: the entry script's job is only to get past the
copyright sequence and the title's MODE A/B menu, and it is the same input
for every value. It therefore lives in defaults.entry and no value
overrides it. It is named mint-city-slum.txt because that is the name the
route's state has to come from (scripts/library_job.py resolves the route
city-slum-run to the longest mint-*.txt that prefixes it, #408), not
because it is specific to Stage 1.
No generator. The brief asks for one where there are many near-identical
mints, and this game has exactly one: four values, one input script, four
pins. A generator that emits a single file with a --check that compares it
to itself is a second copy of the file, not a guard on it, so there is
none and the mint carries its own measurements in its header instead.
_defaultsComment: ADR-0239 s6's budget: 120 emulated seconds, the body repeated to fill the
run. The body is a stage route like any other set's - it walks right into
the stage and attacks - and it presses no START, which on this game would
What that costs, measured on this dump off each session's rec-final.mss:
the selector is pinned for the whole run (ADR-0184's amendment), so every
session starts on its own stage and stays on it - the level-data pointer
does not move for 120 s on any of the four. That is the honest limit of
this set: a blind body does not clear a stage here (Double Dragon's stages
are long, and the body cannot fight its way through one), so the sessions
record the stage's opening material and the checkpoint the stage begins on,
not its later screens. See runs/f1418/doubledragon/RESULT.md for the
Value 00 is the identity: with no pin the game already starts on Stage 1,

_livesComment: No lives pin. ADR-0239 s3 allows one only on a passing inert control - the
pin set to the counter's start value must record a byte-identical
textures/ tree - and on this run that control CANNOT pass. Not an argument:
probe/lives_trace.py reads `$0043` off every state this profile was built
from (exit 0) and the byte takes THREE different values inside every single
session. Pins 00, 01 and 02: 00 at the entry's last frame, 02 once play
begins, then 01, then 00. Pin 03: 01, 00, and FF by 90 s - past the end of
the counter, which is also where `$003D` reads 04, beyond the last stage
the selector names. A pin at the start value would hold a byte the run
otherwise moves, so it is not inert and the control cannot pass; the drift
is the measurement and the failure of the control follows from it.
The control was NOT run. Running a 120 s session to demonstrate the failure
of a test for a pin this profile does not carry would buy nothing, and
saying which of the two it is - read or argued - is the point. What s3 is
actually protecting, that the recorder's cheat machinery must not perturb
the run by itself, IS supplied on the byte that is pinned: 003D:00
substitutes a value that already reads 00, and its released arm is
byte-identical to its held arm, 0 of 2048 RAM bytes differing (probe/
release_test.py).
The candidate codes exist and are published - Almar's Guides gives 0043:04
(Infinite Lives) and 03B4:50 (Infinite health), the vendored database gives
03B4:64 - and none is used.
$0043's drift is also why the check below survives: `$0018` holds 5C/65/7D/
E1 across every row of that table, through the respawns that move `$0043`,
_metricComment: ADR-0239 s4's `new` is drawn keys - (tileData, palette) - and it is the
gate; the builder's `defaultTile` placeholders are excluded, which is what
the 2026-09-26 amendment to s4 says, because on a CHR ROM game the
tile-data string cannot answer s4's question: this ROM's bootstrapped pack
names every CHR index it has, so every session's tile-data set is a subset
of it and `newTiles` is 0. What moves is the drawn key. `[every rule:
100.0%]` in the report is a constant of every bootstrapped pack of this
ROM and must never be quoted as coverage.
